findings.text: Non-root write entry drains and reclaims the target group then reports the request size on success and invalid for root. It resolves the group from the open file and delegates to the internal empty routine, propagating its failure otherwise.

Empty routine first drains global LRU additions and per-group stock, then loops while attempts remain and the memory counter is non-zero. It aborts on pending signal and stops early for a dying group; each iteration tries reclaim with swap permitted and consumes one attempt only on failure, otherwise returning success.
Hierarchy mode is fixed enabled. Read always reports one. Write accepts one and otherwise emits a single deprecation notice and fails, so non-hierarchical operation cannot be selected.

Soft limit is deprecated without effect. Read reports the product of the counter ceiling and page size. Write parses the input but discards it after a single deprecation notice and reports success for the full request.

Generic numeric read selects one of four counters by file type and one of four attributes by file kind. Usage is scaled by page size with memory and combined memory-plus-swap resolved through a usage helper while other counters use the raw count; limit and high watermark are scaled maxima; fail count is raw. Unknown selectors abort.

Generic write handles limit changes after trimming and parsing input. Root limit change is rejected. Memory and combined limits resize the corresponding maxima, kernel memory is a deprecated no-op that warns once and succeeds, and TCP forwards to the TCP maximum updater. Reset clears the high watermark or zeroes the fail count for the selected counter and reports the request size.

TCP maximum update serializes on the maximum mutex. It sets the new TCP ceiling and on first activation enables socket accounting before marking the group active, ordering the flag after the key update so no socket is marked accounted before accounting sites are patched.

Swappiness read returns the effective value. Write rejects values above the global ceiling. Non-root updates the per-group value after a one-time notice that per-group control is absent in v2, while root updates the global value. Success is always reported within range.

OOM control read reports the kill-disable flag, the under-OOM state and the OOM kill event count. Write is deprecated with a single notice, accepts only zero or one on non-root, stores the flag and invokes recovery when clearing to zero.
Two legacy display entries are non-functional. The pressure level display always fails invalid and the slab display always succeeds without emitting output, both retained only for compatibility.

File mask covers inactive and active file lists, anon mask covers inactive and active anon lists, full mask covers all LRU lists, and unevictable is a single bit. Resource selector orders _MEM then _MEMSWAP then _KMEM then _TCP.

Per-node and group-wide LRU counts iterate all LRU kinds, skip kinds outside the supplied mask, and sum either hierarchical or local state. Per-node form resolves the vector for the node and validates the node identifier; group form aggregates across the group. Local versus tree selection controls which state accessor is used.

Local vector state accessor returns node state when the feature is disabled. Otherwise it maps the node statistic to a local index, warns once and returns zero for an unmapped index, and clamps negative percpu drift to zero on SMP before returning.
NUMA display flushes group statistics then prints local totals followed by hierarchical totals for total, file, anon and unevictable classes, each with a group total and a per memory-node breakdown.

Version one statistics map internal counters to names cache, rss, rss_huge when huge pages are enabled, shmem, mapped_file, dirty, writeback, workingset_refault_anon, workingset_refault_file, plus swap and swapcached when swap is enabled. Event counters track page in, page out, faults and major faults.

Reparent helpers transfer local accounting to the parent by reading the child local value and applying equal negative and positive deltas. One helper moves a single group statistic, one iterates the version one statistic set, one iterates all LRU lists per node through per-node containers, and a group LRU variant walks every node.

Legacy control tables define user-visible names and operations. Core names are usage_in_bytes, max_usage_in_bytes, limit_in_bytes, soft_limit_in_bytes, failcnt, stat, force_empty, use_hierarchy, cgroup.event_control without prefix, swappiness, move_charge_at_immigrate, oom_control, pressure_level and conditional numa_stat; kernel names add kmem variants and conditional kmem.slabinfo; TCP names add kmem.tcp variants; swap names add memsw variants for combined memory-plus-swap usage, peak, limit and fail count.

Socket charging attempts the TCP counter and on success clears pressure and reports true. On failure it sets pressure; no-fail allocations force the charge and still report true, otherwise it reports false. Uncharge releases the counter and the active flag reports whether TCP accounting is enabled, with disabled builds always inactive and charging always succeeding.
Event storage allocates an accounted percpu block and reports presence, and frees it on teardown. Disabled builds provide inline fallbacks that always report success and do nothing.

Global state holds the memory subsystem and root group as mostly-read data, a percpu interrupt-active pointer, socket, kernel memory and BPF disable flags plus the workqueue as read-only after init, slab caches for groups and per-node structures, a four kilobyte sequence buffer size, an object charging update bit zero with its flag as one shifted by that bit, and a spinlock guarding object charging structures. Tracepoints are enabled in this unit.

Boot initialization allocates a per-node soft-limit tree entry on its node, sets an empty tree with no rightmost entry and initializes its lock. Soft-limit reset restores the counter ceiling, with a no-op fallback when disabled alongside no-op fallbacks for group init, tree removal, offline, OOM recovery, charge commit and batch uncharge. Header guard defines the version one interface inclusion marker.
Object charging uses a dedicated spinlock, and each per-node soft-limit tree carries its own lock initialized at boot alongside the empty tree state.

Limit changes on the root group, hierarchy disable attempts, out-of-range swappiness, and OOM control changes on root or outside zero and one are rejected. Several legacy controls warn once about removal and either ignore the write or retain prior behavior, so callers cannot rely on them for enforcement.
